content.title: St. John's University SAT, ACT & GPA Admission Requirements
content.text: St. John's University, located at the dynamic heartbeat of New York, is known for its academic programs and well-rounded, dynamic campus life. Life around undergraduates and graduate students is one of constant intellectual and personal growth. For this reason, understanding and being fully aware of SAT and GPA requirements at St. John's University averts the odds of your matriculation. The acceptance rate at St. John's University is hovering around 80 per cent, making it a fair game since approximately 70 per cent of the applicants get accepted. Admitted students are mainly in the 50th percentile with an SAT score ranging from 1150 to 1330, an ACT score of 24 to 29, and a GPA ranging from 3.5 to 4.00. Strong academic background at St. John's will be complemented by good extracurricular work and a well-thought-out personal statement. Continue reading for a comprehensive guide on preparing a competitive application to Saint John's University, and assess whether the SAT and GPA align with your strengths.🎓 Did You Know These Facts About St. John's University? A Historic Beginning: St. John's University was founded way back in 1870 by the Vincentian Fathers. It started as a small Catholic institution in Brooklyn before moving to its current campus in Queens in 1955. Mascot Overhaul: The university's mascot has evolved over the years. Initially, they used "Chief Blackjack," a cigar store Indian adopted in 1928, but it was retired for cultural reasons. In 1994, Johnny Thunderbird became the new mascot, representing the school's lively spirit and energy. Famous Alumni: St. John's University has produced some big names, from NBA stars like Metta World Peace and Chris Mullin, to Grammy-winning rapper J. Cole, and even former New York Governor Mario Cuomo. Global Reach: St. John's isn't just based in New York—students have the chance to study abroad at campuses in Rome and Paris, adding an international dimension to their academic experience. Community Leader: One of the most significant roles that Joseph Sciame, fondly known as "Mr. St. John's," has played for more than 60 years is the shaping of the university's community programs and financial aid initiatives. His historical impact resonates forever within the school. Details Information College Name St. John's University College Location Queens, New York College Short Form SJU Acceptance Rate 80% Graduation Rate 79% FAFSA Deadline February 15 Early Decision November 1 Regular Application Due January 15 Common Application Accepted Yes SAT Score 1150-1330 ACT Score 24-29 Roles of SAT and GPA in Admission at St. John's University St. John's University is not going to straightforwardly deny children just on the basis of their SAT scores or GPA; it's going to weigh the same with everything else it has to offer. St. John's University emphasises competitive SAT, ACT, and GPA scores for admission. Besides this, the institution looks into several other important things, including extracurricular activities, leadership positions, letters of recommendation, and personal essays. All of these things could go a long way in increasing your chances of getting into St. John's University.St. John's University Admission RequirementsSt. John's University is committed to selecting exceptional students based on academic merit and leadership potential. In addition to meeting the St. John's University SAT requirements and maintaining a good GPA, the university values applicants who demonstrate passion and excellence in their chosen disciplines and extracurricular activities. Requirement Status Details High School GPA Required; preference for strong academic performance Applicants are generally expected to have a GPA of 3.5 or higher; competitive candidates typically possess a GPA between 3.6-4.0+. High School Rank Considered but not required A strong class rank can enhance an application, particularly for competitive candidates. SAT/ACT Scores Optional; test-optional policy St. John's University SAT requirements are optional, but high scores can still strengthen an application. Letters of Recommendation Required; recommended two to three letters Recommendations from teachers or mentors provide insights into the applicant's academic and leadership abilities. Personal Statement Required: opportunity to showcase personal strengths The personal essay allows applicants to highlight their unique experiences, values, and aspirations. Application Fee $75 (subject to change) The fee is non-refundable; applicants should check St. John's University's website for updates on fees. Extracurricular Activities Strongly encouraged Active participation in clubs, sports, or community service enhances an application and demonstrates leadership qualities. Interviews Optional Interviews may provide additional context about the applicant; not required, but beneficial. AP/IB Courses Recommended Taking Advanced Placement (AP) or International Baccalaureate (IB) courses demonstrates academic rigour. Portfolio (for specific programs) Required for certain majors Applicants to particular programs may need to submit a portfolio. How to Write a Winning Admission Application to St. John's University A sincere application is what will win you a place at St. John's University. Impressions on the admissions committee will depend on how personal and open you are in sharing your experiences, reasons, and objectives. The application will become very stiff and strong with some letters of recommendation and a very balanced profile of achievements, leadership positions, and involvement in extracurricular activities. Tips for a Compelling Application to St. John's University: Be honest and authentic when describing your experiences. Ensure your statement reflects your journey and goals. Highlight significant extracurricular activities and leadership roles you've held. Obtain strong letters of recommendation from teachers or mentors. Mention any advanced coursework, such as AP or IB classes. Demonstrate a clear interest in attending St. John's University in your application. Show how you have contributed to your community. Ensure your application highlights your strengths across multiple areas. Proofread your application for typos or errors and submit it well before the deadline. St. John's University SAT Requirements Although the Saint John's University SAT requirements are optional due to the test-optional policy, submitting competitive SAT scores can help strengthen your application. These scores are often seen as an indicator of a student's preparedness for the rigorous academic work at St. John's University. Average SAT Scores for Admitted Students at St. John's University The middle 50% of students admitted to St. John's University have SAT scores between 1150 and 1330. Specifically, Evidence-Based Reading and Writing (EBRW) scores range from 580-670, and Math scores range from 570-610. While strong Saint John's University SAT requirements are essential, St. John's University employs a holistic review process that also considers GPA, extracurricular involvement, and personal essays. St. John's University SAT Scores Distribution The average SAT score for admitted students at St. John's University is approximately 1,245. The middle 50% of admitted students have SAT scores ranging from 1,150 to 1,330. For the Evidence-Based Reading and Writing (EBRW) section, the middle 50% scored between 580 and 670, while in Math, the range was between 570 and 670. St. John's University also has an optional admissions testing policy, where applicants are not required to present their SAT scores, but could enhance their profile. More sensitive applicants to competitive programs should submit SAT scores at least at the mean score or higher. John's University's SAT requirements require focused preparation and effective time management. Here are some tips to help you improve your SAT scores: Identify your weak areas in the SAT sections and target those for improvement. Use high-quality SAT prep materials, including practice tests. Practice under timed conditions to simulate test day pressure. Create a consistent study schedule and adhere to it. Consider seeking external help through tutoring or SAT prep courses if needed. St. John's University ACT Requirements Different colleges have different priorities in determining their admission candidates. It is notable that his holistic consideration of ACT scores has assumed a central place in St. John's University. St. John's University ACT Scores St. John's University offers flexibility in its admissions process by making ACT scores optional. However, submitting ACT scores can provide additional insights into a student's academic abilities. Applicants who choose to submit ACT scores should aim for results that reflect their preparedness for the rigorous academic environment at St. John's University. Average St. John's University ACT Scores for Accepted Students The middle 50% of students admitted to St. John's University have ACT scores between 24 and 29. Specifically, composite scores range from 25-30, with individual section scores reflecting strong performance across all areas. While ACT scores are optional, meeting the Saint. John's University's SAT requirements can enhance an applicant's profile. Percentile ACT Score 25th 24 50% Middle 27 75th 29 St. John's University ACT Score Ranges St. John's University usually expects competitive scores on the ACT from its applicants, with admitted students usually falling in the higher percentiles of test-takers. The middle 50% ACT score for admissions typically at St. John's University ranged between 24 and 29, which strongly reinforces its academic prestige; thus, a composite score within this range puts candidates in a good position for consideration. St. John's University does not simply consider ACT scores in its holistic approach to admission. This is one type of academic inputs: academic performance, extramural activities, and personal traits form a well-rounded applicant profile. John's University ACT requirements require focused preparation and effective time management. Here are some tips to help you improve your ACT scores: Identify your weak areas in ACT sections and target those for improvement. Use high-quality ACT prep materials, including practice tests. Practice under timed conditions to simulate test day pressure. Create a consistent study schedule and adhere to it. Consider seeking external help through tutoring or ACT prep courses if needed. St. John's University GPA Requirements The student's GPA remains a critical variable in St. John's University admission procedures. A good GPA shows that the student has consistently performed and is ready for the difficult work taken at the university. GPA Requirement at St. John's University Most admitted students at St. John's University have GPAs ranging from 3.5 to 4.0. While St. John's University does not have a strict minimum GPA requirement, applicants with higher GPAs are generally more competitive. Applicants with GPAs below 3.5 may find it challenging to compete unless they excel in other areas of the application. Average GPA of Admitted Students The middle 50% of students admitted to St. John's University have an average GPA between 3.5 and 4.0 on a 4.0 scale. If your GPA is lower, ensure that other parts of your application are strong to compensate. GPA Percentile GPA Range 25th 3.5 75th 4.0+ St. John's University Acceptance Rate St. John's University (SJU) is moderately selective, with an acceptance rate of approximately 80%. For the most recent admissions cycle, SJU received around 24,000 applications, and 20,196 students were admitted. Given its competitive nature, applicants are encouraged to submit strong personal statements, showcase leadership in extracurricular activities, and demonstrate academic excellence to increase their chances of acceptance. Key Points Details Total Applicants Approximately 24,208 Admitted Students 20,196 Enrolled 2,350 Scholarships at St. John's University St. John's University offers a variety of scholarships to help students finance their education. These scholarships include merit-based awards, need-based aid, and specific opportunities for graduate students and those studying abroad. Whether you're an incoming freshman or a graduate student, there are numerous options to make your education more affordable. Merit-Based Scholarships: Automatically awarded to first-year students based on academic performance. No separate application needed. Catholic High School Scholarship: $3,000 annually for students from Catholic high schools. Graduate Scholarships: Various scholarships are available for graduate students based on academic excellence and program requirements. Study Abroad Scholarships: These include the Licari Scholarship (up to $1,000) and the Giambelli Scholarship for international internships and study abroad. Need-Based Aid: Financial aid awarded based on the FAFSA application. Saint John's University Test-Optional Admissions Policy St. John's University is test-optional when it comes to admission, enabling all first-year applicants to decide whether to submit SAT or ACT scores. The admissions process thus emphasises a holistic review that takes into account GPA from high school, course difficulty, extracurricular activities, personal essays, and letters of recommendation. Applicants with SAT scores below 1050 or ACT scores below 23 are encouraged to apply test-optional, as standardised test scores may not accurately reflect their academic potential. However, specific programs, like the Biology (with NYIT Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine Pathway Opportunity), require standardised test scores for admission. The test-optional application is also open to international applicants coming from English-speaking countries, with the condition that certain English language proficiency requirements must have been met. Decisions regarding test-optional applications are final and cannot be altered once the application form is submitted.Conclusion Admission to St. John's University requires a high level of academic achievement, including competitive SAT scores and GPA. However, getting good grades may not be enough to be accepted. Leadership, extracurricular activities, and essays that provide personal insight are the additional essentials of an application that would heighten your chances. Students who excel across all aspects of the application process are more likely to gain admission to this esteemed university.Check Colleges Accepting Low ACT Scores Colleges That Accept a 1200 Score on the SAT
